task_brief: Day 7 of "Music Composition, Production, and Performance" (unit 3, grade 8) is an investigation on rhythm harmony and melody. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Compose or arrange an original short work and present it live, recorded, sequenced, or through a detailed score/listening map. Today's work contributes to that by handling rhythm harmony and melody at the investigation or close reading stage, against the unit's wider topics of rhythm harmony and melody, form and arrangement, notation or digital sequencing, and recording and mixing concepts. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Closely examine a work you did not make that demonstrates rhythm harmony and melody. Describe before you judge: what is present, how it is organised, and what happens over time or across the surface. Then interpret — what effect is created, and which specific element creates it. Support every claim with something a reader could check in the work itself. Finish with one question the work raises that you cannot answer from it alone. Use only public-domain, openly licensed, or properly cited works, and quote or excerpt no more than you need to make the point. Use the attached Academy-original reference work as the work under investigation; no outside artwork, recording, performance, or web source is required. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about rhythm harmony and melody, and it belongs to "Music Composition, Production, and Performance", which also covers separate topics such as form and arrangement. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about rhythm harmony and melody; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.

sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g8-arts-and-music-u03-l07

Lesson focus: rhythm harmony and melody

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_REFERENCE_WORK

REFERENCE WORK — "Returning Steps," a text-notated micro-composition. Pulse: 1 2 3 4 | 1 2 3 4. Rhythm: TA TI-TI TA rest | TA-A TI-TI TA. Optional pitches: C D E G | G E D C. Dynamics: soft for beats 1–4, medium for beats 5–7, soft on beat 8. Form: opening rise, held arrival, return. Use it to study rhythm harmony and melody; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-original reference work as the work under investigation; no outside artwork, recording, performance, or web source is required.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: Description precedes judgement, covering what is present and how it is organised.
Every interpretive claim points to something checkable in the work itself.
The specific element creating the effect is identified rather than the effect only named.
One unanswerable question raised by the work is stated.
Sources are public domain, openly licensed, or properly cited, and excerpts are no longer than the point requires.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres an aural element (rhythm harmony and melody). Provide a fully equivalent non-aural route: notated, written, or graphic representation; visual or tactile pulse (a moving marker, a tapped or felt beat); and vibration or sight-reading in place of listening. Do not require the learner to hear a pitch, interval, or timbre to demonstrate understanding of it.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for rhythm harmony and melody follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for rhythm harmony and melody, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for rhythm harmony and melody works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of rhythm harmony and melody, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking rhythm harmony and melody mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply rhythm harmony and melody under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on rhythm harmony and melody rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
